name: Proximal Hamstring Tendinopathy Rehabilitation Protocol
description: Evidence-based 12-week protocol for proximal hamstring tendinopathy with focus on avoiding stretching and progressive loading
pain_rule: Pain max. 3/10 during the exercise. Avoid deep hamstring stretching and prolonged sitting.
evidence_base: Goom et al. (2016): Proximal hamstring tendinopathy management protocol
Puranen & Orava (1988): Athletic hamstring injury classification
Fredericson et al. (2005): High hamstring tendinopathy in runners
Cook & Purdam (2009): Compressive load management in tendinopathy
progression_criteria: Hip hinge with 70% bodyweight as added load without pain
No pain during brisk walking or light jogging

exercises.name: Isometric Hamstring Bridge
exercises.description: Supine, heels on elevated surface (chair/bench). Lift hips and hold
exercises.phase_goal: Pain reduction and hamstring activation without compression

exercises.name: Isometric Prone Leg Curl
exercises.description: Prone, knee bent to 45 degrees. Press heel against a firm surface
exercises.phase_goal: Pain reduction and hamstring activation without compression

exercises.name: Hip Hinge (Romanian Deadlift)
exercises.description: Standing, dumbbells in front of thighs. Push hips back, keep back straight
exercises.phase_goal: Strengthen hamstring tendon without excessive compression

exercises.name: Hamstring Bridge Slide
exercises.description: Supine, heels on sliders. Slowly extend legs and pull back
exercises.phase_goal: Strengthen hamstring tendon without excessive compression

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift
exercises.description: Standing on one leg, lean upper body forward. Use dumbbells or kettlebell
exercises.phase_goal: Strengthen hamstring tendon without excessive compression

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl (Assisted)
exercises.description: Kneeling, feet fixed. Slowly lower upper body forward, catch with hands
exercises.phase_goal: Eccentric load tolerance and return to sporting activities

exercises.name: Sprinter Lunge
exercises.description: Lunge with upper body leaning forward. Powerfully drive back leg forward
exercises.phase_goal: Eccentric load tolerance and return to sporting activities
